transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Brien (CSM), Michael Torres (CISO, Evergreen), Samantha Lee (IT Ops), Daniel Kim (Security Eng), Ava Walker (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick security/compliance review focused on audit logs and admin activity: what Redwood captures, export options (S3, syslog, API), retention controls, KMS/encryption, RBAC/SSO integration, and proof artifacts (SOC2/ISO). Customer asked about long-term retention and immutable exports for legal holds.

Topics:
- Audit log fields and event types captured
- Export/destination options and formats
- Retention windows and legal hold
- Encryption at rest and KMS integration
- RBAC and SSO activity logging
- Demo request for sample export and schema

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll hand it to Priya to walk through the audit log coverage we have and then we'll go through retention and exports, and then Q&A.
[00:12] Priya Patel: Yep thanks Jordan. So Redwood's audit logs capture admin actions, user logins, token creates/rotates, model deploys, rollout changes, API key events, and data-export events. Also some infra events like node restarts, but less granular there.
[00:28] Michael Torres: When you say admin actions, can you be specific, like delete user vs change role? We need immutable evidence for audits.
[00:35] Priya Patel: Yeah good q. We capture change type (create/update/delete), actor ID, actor email, IP, timestamp, resource id, and before/after where feasible. For example role changes show previous role and new role in the event payload. The before/after sometimes is truncated for very large configs — but that's rare.
[00:50] Samantha Lee: Are these logs tied into SSO events? We use SAML via Okta.
[00:56] Priya Patel: SSO events are logged — SAML assertions, successful and failed logins, session durations. We ingest the IdP event id when available, so you can correlate. There are occasional transcription mismatches for some IdP fields, but we're pretty consistent.
[01:12] Daniel Kim: What's the retention default and what are options for extended retention? We might need 7 years for certain records.
[01:20] Priya Patel: Default retention for audit logs on hosted accounts is 90 days. For Dedicated and Private deployments, retention is configurable; we offer 1 year and multi-year retention as an add-on and for Private you can manage retention in your own object store. For hosted long-retention we can route exports to your S3 bucket with lifecycle rules.
[01:38] Michael Torres: If we export to S3, can we ensure immutability / legal hold?
[01:42] Priya Patel: Yes, you can configure S3 object lock on your bucket to enforce WORM. Redwood will deliver the files via our export job to your target; the immutability is enforced by the destination policy. We also support streaming to SIEMs such as Splunk or Datadog via syslog/HTTP.
[02:00] Jordan Meyers: To add — for compliance we can provide signed manifests for export batches so you have evidence of integrity, plus checksums.
[02:08] Ava Walker: Signed manifests would be useful. Also need to know what levels of encryption and KMS control we have; our data residency rules require customer-managed keys.
[02:19] Priya Patel: For hosted we support customer-managed KMS (CMK) via AWS KMS or Cloud HSM integrations. You can bring your key and we do envelope encryption: data encrypted with a data key, which is encrypted by your CMK. For Private, you manage keys completely in your environment.
[02:38] Samantha Lee: Are audit logs encrypted at rest in the same way as user data?
[02:42] Priya Patel: Yes, audit logs are encrypted at rest. The same KMS settings apply to logs and stored artifacts. For S3 exports we recommend server-side encryption using your CMK (SSE-KMS) or client-side encryption if you require it.
[02:55] Daniel Kim: How about tamper detection? You mentioned checksums — any option for signing per-record?
[03:03] Priya Patel: We don't sign every individual event with a crypto signature out-of-the-box, but we produce batch manifests with SHA256 checksums for each file and we can enable append-only storage patterns. For higher assurance, on Private deployments we can integrate with your internal signing service if needed.
[03:20] Michael Torres: Ok...we have to map this to SOC2 Type II requirements and show evidence of admin activity. Do you have templates?
[03:26] Liam O'Brien: We do — Jordan will share the SOC2 and ISO certs and a compliance pack that outlines mapping of audit events to typical control families.
[03:33] Jordan Meyers: Yep I'll share those after the call.
[03:36] Samantha Lee: Format question — what export formats do you support? CSV? JSON? Parquet?
[03:41] Priya Patel: Exports support newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) and CSV for smaller schemas. For larger workloads we can do Parquet and partition by date. API pulls are also available for near-real-time streaming.
[03:54] Daniel Kim: For NDJSON, is there a schema? We need field-level mapping into our SIEM.
[03:58] Priya Patel: There's a canonical schema — I'll attach it. Fields include event_type, timestamp, actor_id, actor_email, actor_ip, resource_type, resource_id, action, outcome, details. Some events have nested JSON in the details field (e.g., before/after) — it's stringified in CSV exports which can cause parsing pain.
[04:19] Michael Torres: Nested fields are fine if JSON is kept — we prefer NDJSON. CSV can lose context.
[04:24] Priya Patel: Agreed. For compliance, NDJSON is recommended.
[04:27] Jordan Meyers: Any concerns around PII in logs? We try to avoid capturing full payloads.
[04:32] Daniel Kim: We need clarity on what user data you log — IPs are okay but not full request payloads.
[04:36] Priya Patel: Redwood by default redacts sensitive request/response bodies from audit logs and only logs metadata. For customers who need deeper traces for debugging, there's an opt-in debug capture with strict retention and access controls, and that can be disabled for compliance.
[04:52] Samantha Lee: What about SSO/SAML failures — do you log assertion contents?
[04:57] Priya Patel: We log event metadata and assertion IDs; we do not persist full assertions by default. If you want assertion payloads for a short troubleshooting window, we can enable that but it's not stored long term.
[05:10] Michael Torres: Can we get audit logs into our SIEM in near real-time? Latency matters for security detection.
[05:15] Priya Patel: Yes, near-real-time streaming via webhooks or Kafka (for Dedicated) is supported. For hosted we provide a streaming API or push to your HTTP endpoint. Typical latency is sub-30s, depends on throughput.
[05:28] Daniel Kim: For Dedicated, can we have VPC peering and private endpoints for the stream?
[05:32] Priya Patel: Yes — Dedicated supports VPC peering, private links, and you can host the export sink inside your VPC.
[05:39] Jordan Meyers: Just to note, some customers use a hybrid: short-term retention in Redwood for quick lookups and long-term WORM in S3 for audits.
[05:48] Ava Walker: That model would work for us. Need to confirm retention windows and cost.
[05:52] Priya Patel: We'll share a cost estimate for the long-retention add-on. Also, retention versus searchability is a trade-off: long-term archived data can be partitioned and restored for queries, but you pay retrieval costs.
[06:06] Samantha Lee: How do you handle admin impersonation or service accounts? We have service accounts that do automation; need clear labeling.
[06:13] Priya Patel: Service accounts are labeled and we capture the token id and owner. We also capture if action was via API vs console.
[06:19] Daniel Kim: Any RBAC granularity? e.g., per-route permissions and auditability per role?
[06:25] Priya Patel: Our RBAC supports role-based policies and custom roles. Audit logs record role bindings and policy changes. For Private deployments you can integrate with your central RBAC system.
[06:36] Michael Torres: For SOC2 evidence we need 1) logs of role changes, 2) login failures, 3) privileged actions. Sounds like you cover those.
[06:45] Jordan Meyers: Correct — we can produce that mapping in the compliance pack.
[06:48] Daniel Kim: On encryption, if we bring our KMS, who has access to the keys?
[06:52] Priya Patel: With CMK you control key policies. Redwood never gets the unencrypted CMK. We request decrypt/encrypt permissions as needed via IAM role, per standard AWS KMS practice. For on-prem or HSM we can do different integration patterns.
[07:10] Ava Walker: Are audit logs included in your SOC2 scope?
[07:14] Liam O'Brien: Yes, audit logging and monitoring are included in our SOC2 Type II audit; we'll send the relevant section.
[07:20] Samantha Lee: Will you share retention SLAs and if there are any gaps for compliance?
[07:24] Jordan Meyers: We'll share retention SLAs for hosted and Dedicated, and outline what Private customers manage themselves.
[07:29] Priya Patel: Quick note on schemas — sometimes product names get mangled in transcriptions (e.g., Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood degrad—) that's a transcription thing, not the product.
[07:41] Michael Torres: Haha noted.
[07:44] Daniel Kim: For exports and integrity, can you attach a signed manifest and a PGP signature per batch?
[07:49] Priya Patel: We can provide manifest + checksum; PGP signing per batch is an engineering ask but feasible for customers with high assurance needs — we'll scope in the deep dive.
[08:02] Samantha Lee: For legal hold, how fast can you trigger an export if we need to preserve data?
[08:07] Priya Patel: We can trigger an on-demand export job and push to S3; typical job completion for a 90-day window is minutes to an hour depending on volume. For multi-year archives it could take longer but still workable.
[08:21] Michael Torres: Good.
[08:23] Jordan Meyers: Any other open items?
[08:25] Ava Walker: Can you provide a sample NDJSON export so we can map fields?
[08:29] Priya Patel: Yes, I'll attach a sample file and the schema.
[08:33] Daniel Kim: Also want a short runbook for incident response — how to pull logs and correlate quickly.
[08:39] Liam O'Brien: We'll prep an incident runbook template for Evergreen.
[08:43] Jordan Meyers: Cool. We'll summarize next steps.
[08:47] Michael Torres: One last Q — are admin actions timestamped in UTC and do you include timezone offsets?
[08:52] Priya Patel: All timestamps are ISO8601 in UTC, and we include original timezone info when available in the metadata.
[08:58] Samantha Lee: Thanks everyone.

Recap & Next steps (verbatim from call):
- Jordan to share SOC2 Type II and ISO certs + compliance pack (by 2026-04-13).
- Priya to send audit log schema, sample NDJSON export, and S3 export config (by 2026-04-15).
- Customer (Daniel) to confirm retention windows and legal hold requirements (by 2026-04-14).

End of transcript.
